clue.text: Failures the learner dismissed in the recesses

indicators.note: the learner being dismissed means that letter is sent out of the word for failures

parts.note: lapses are failures or slips
L is the learner, as on an L-plate

explanation.surface: A teacher sends a struggling student out of the alcoves where the failures are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: APSES are the semicircular recesses at the end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess in a church, so the plural gives recesses.

clue.text: Showing anxiety relating to understanding

definitions.meaning: fearful that something bad will happen
concerned with grasping or perceiving, as in the mind's power of apprehension

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both anxious and, in an older sense, to do with mental grasp or perception.

clue.text: Takes advance payments to include pamphlet

indicators.note: one piece is made to include the other, so the pamphlet goes inside

parts.note: subs are advances on wages, or subscriptions paid ahead
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: Someone collects payments in advance and slips a leaflet in with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtracts means takes away, as in takes three from ten.

clue.text: Stylish thrash

definitions.meaning: smart and fashionable, a British informal sense
to beat or lash, as with a cane that whistles through the air

explanation.definitionFit: Swish is British slang for posh or stylish, and as a verb means to lash or beat with a cane.

clue.text: Final offers made by university officer to one academic with thanks

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an army officer
I is the Roman numeral for one
an MA, a Master of Arts, is an academic
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A college official presents final terms to a lecturer and thanks them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimata is a Latin plural of ultimatum, a last offer or demand before action is taken.

clue.text: Kind of NUS files hard to unravel

indicators.note: the letters are left to unravel and come apart into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The National Union of Students has records that are difficult to sort out.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students; here its letters are only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An unselfish person is kind, putting others first; synonym.

clue.text: We hear the side is to come down heavily

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the spelling changes but the sound stays

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Rumour has it the team is about to drop heavily in the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Teem means to pour with rain, which is to come down heavily.

clue.text: Earn money in preparation for printing

parts.note: to make money is to earn it
the ready is informal for cash, as in ready money

explanation.surface: Someone earns cash while preparing a print run.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-ready is the printers' term for adjusting a press before a run, its preparation for printing.

clue.text: Number wearing old garment seen in the South Pacific

indicators.note: the number wears the garment, so the garment goes round it

parts.note: the toga was the robe of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A figure in Roman dress turns up on a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom located in the South Pacific Ocean; the definition is descriptive.

clue.text: Platform announcements?

parts.note: suggests messages heard at a railway station, but means talks given from a speaker's stage to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: Addressing an audience from a stage or platform is the art of oratory.

clue.text: One used to avoid getting the ticket

definitions.text: One used to avoid getting the ticket

parts.words: One used to avoid getting the ticket
parts.note: the ticket sounds like something bought for travel, but it is a fine for leaving a car without paying

explanation.definitionFit: Paying a roadside coin machine lets a driver stay legally and escape a fine.

clue.text: Liar they put right in a crude way

indicators.note: the letters are put right, that is set in their correct order anew

explanation.surface: A liar and others are corrected for speaking coarsely.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthily means in a coarse, down-to-earth manner, a synonym for crudely.

clue.text: An artist takes in abandoned ships

parts.note: an means a

indicators.note: one piece takes the other in, enclosing it

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
abandoned behaviour is wild and unrestrained, so mad

explanation.surface: A painter adopts some derelict vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, so ships in quantity.

clue.text: Use endless charity when performing church service

indicators.note: performing as in carrying out a routine or trick, so the letters do a turn
the word is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Advice to draw on charity in a church setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final Y of charity, giving CHARIT, which joins USE for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian service of Holy Communion.

clue.text: Broadcaster ran out without part of speech on the Church

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters surround the rest
out here means disordered, so the letters of ran are rearranged
in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a noun is one of the parts of speech
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A broadcaster fled without saying anything about the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'out' scrambles the letters of ran to ANR.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer reads news or links programmes on radio or television, a broadcaster.

clue.text: Persistent cautions and police finally move

indicators.note: the letters are made to move into a fresh arrangement
finally picks the final letter of police

explanation.surface: Police issue warnings and then tell people to move along, doggedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacious means holding on firmly, a synonym for persistent.

clue.text: A footballer can be taken thus

parts.note: a back is a defender in football

explanation.surface: A player can be caught out this way.
explanation.walkthrough: One can be taken aback, meaning surprised; the clue asks how one can be taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken aback is the idiom for startled, so the word completes the phrase.

clue.text: Simultaneously make good and raise issue

parts.note: to atone is to make amends, make good

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: Someone makes amends and brings up a matter in the same breath.
explanation.definitionFit: At one time can mean together or at once, a synonym for simultaneously.

clue.text: Reverse for students, including a society girl

indicators.note: reverse tells us the whole built piece is read backwards
the students including the rest means those letters go inside

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: The student union backtracks and admits a socialite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts AS inside NUS for NASUS, which 'Reverse' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a girl's name; crosswords often define a name by a generic word.

clue.text: Darling American goes on dream holiday

parts.note: honey is an endearment typical of American speech
to moon is to daydream

explanation.surface: An American sweetheart heads off on a perfect break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' is a link: the second piece follows the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the holiday a couple take after marrying.

clue.text: Minister backs Brown in old battle

indicators.note: the minister backs, that is goes backwards

parts.note: Rev is a reverend, a minister
dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A cleric supports a man named Brown in a historic conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdun was the long First World War battle of 1916 in France.

clue.text: Band thrown up in cooler, lacking a leader

indicators.note: the word loses its leading letter, the first one

parts.note: a fridge is a refrigerator, a cooler

explanation.surface: A strip is regurgitated inside an icebox missing its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a raised strip, a band of ground or material pushed upwards.

clue.text: Hard stuff's the best for a brick, perhaps

parts.note: ice is water frozen hard
the cream is the best part, as in cream of the crop

explanation.surface: The strongest material is best for building with bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: A brick here is a block of ice cream, as sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A brick is one example of a frozen dessert sold in a rectangular block.

clue.text: Rag? Worthless stuff!

definitions.meaning: to tease or banter with someone
husks separated from grain, so rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is both light-hearted teasing and the useless husks left after threshing.

clue.text: Spot of inflammation I saw in speech

definitions.text: Spot of inflammation I saw in speech

parts.words: Spot of inflammation I saw in speech
parts.note: a sore swelling on the eyelid, and I saw said out loud gives eyesore, which such a spot is

explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a red spot of inflammation.

clue.text: Teacher disseminated Latin — a citation's due!

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered widely, so the letters are spread out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher spread Latin around, citing it as only fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin is abbreviated to L; only that letter joins A CITATIONS DUE for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An educationalist is an expert in or practitioner of teaching, so a teacher.

clue.text: A much smaller number touring the East for game

indicators.note: the larger piece tours round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: far less means a much smaller number
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Fewer people travel round the East to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means brave and willing, a synonym for fearless.

clue.text: Less restricted, as eggs can be: the last four being off

indicators.note: the final four letters go off, removed from the end

parts.note: eggs can be free-range, from hens allowed outdoors

explanation.surface: Eggs can come from freer hens, but four of the last batch have gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Freer is the comparative of free, meaning less restricted.
